fields.name: open
fields.doc: Which unknowns this exchange is to settle. At least one, or there is nothing to ask.

fields.name: askedOf
fields.doc: Who is being asked. The two participant kinds are symmetric — the same skill serves human-to-agent and agent-to-agent — but the answer's weight differs, so the kind is recorded rather than inferred.

fields.name: candidates

fields.name: context

decls.name: DiscussionInput.askedOf

fields.name: url
fields.doc: Clone URL or path. Not required to be reachable — a Bootstrapping Agent may have been told about a repository it cannot yet fetch.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: Which part this repository plays. A flat list loses the distinction, and the distinction is the whole reason for determining them: it is where the new declaration lands.

decls.name: DiscussionOutput
decls.doc: What the exchange determined: which harness, which repositories, on whose word, and by what means. This document existing and conforming is what finishes the task — not that a conversation took place.

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc: `unsettled` is a real outcome, not an error: a participant may decline, and the process has an end for it. What an `unsettled` result must never contain is a guess.

fields.name: harness
fields.doc: The harness this repository is to become — `bootstrap`, or any Harness built on it. Required when `outcome` is `settled` and `harness` was open.

fields.name: repositories
fields.doc: The repositories involved, each with the part it plays. Recorded as pairs rather than a flat list: read-from and written-to may be one repository or two, and which is which is the answer.

fields.name: determinedBy
fields.doc: `asked` means a participant said so. `assumed` is permitted only for a default the README itself states, and then `assumption` must say which. An agent that reaches for `assumed` because nobody answered has produced an `unsettled` result, not an assumed one.

fields.name: assumption
fields.doc: Required when `determinedBy` is `assumed`: the documented default relied on, and where it is stated.

fields.name: answeredBy
fields.doc: Who settled it. An answer from a sibling agent is evidence of a different weight from the person who wants the harness — both are admissible, neither is conflated with the other.

fields.name: exchange
fields.doc: What was actually put and what came back, in order. One entry is the expected case — the skill's rule is to ask the fewest questions that settle it.

fields.name: stillOpen
fields.doc: Required in substance when `outcome` is `unsettled`: what remains undetermined, so the next actor resumes rather than restarts.

decls.name: oa
decls.doc: properties oa states no domain in its own classes for

fields.name: oa:annotationService
fields.doc: The object of the relationship is the end point of a service that conforms to the annotation-protocol, and it may be associated with any resource.  The expectation of asserting the relationship is that the object is the preferred service for maintaining annotations about the subject resource, according to the publisher of the relationship.

fields.name: oa:canonical
fields.doc: A object of the relationship is the canonical IRI that can always be used to deduplicate the Annotation, regardless of the current IRI used to access the representation.

fields.name: oa:end
fields.doc: The end property is used to convey the 0-based index of the end position of a range of content.

fields.name: oa:exact
fields.doc: The object of the predicate is a copy of the text which is being selected, after normalization.

fields.name: oa:hasPurpose
fields.doc: The purpose served by the resource in the Annotation.

fields.name: oa:prefix
fields.doc: The object of the property is a snippet of content that occurs immediately before the content which is being selected by the Selector.

fields.name: oa:processingLanguage
fields.doc: The object of the property is the language that should be used for textual processing algorithms when dealing with the content of the resource, including hyphenation, line breaking, which font to use for rendering and so forth.  The value must follow the recommendations of BCP47.

fields.name: oa:refinedBy
fields.doc: The relationship between a Selector and another Selector or a State and a Selector or State that should be applied to the results of the first to refine the processing of the source resource.

fields.name: oa:start
fields.doc: The start position in a 0-based index at which a range of content is selected from the data in the source resource.

fields.name: oa:suffix
fields.doc: The snippet of text that occurs immediately after the text which is being selected.

fields.name: oa:textDirection
fields.doc: The direction of the text of the subject resource. There MUST only be one text direction associated with any given resource.

fields.name: oa:via
fields.doc: A object of the relationship is a resource from which the source resource was retrieved by the providing system.

decls.name: oa:Annotation
decls.doc: The class for Web Annotations.

fields.name: oa:bodyValue
fields.doc: The object of the predicate is a plain text string to be used as the content of the body of the Annotation.  The value MUST be an  xsd:string  and that data type MUST NOT be expressed in the serialization. Note that language MUST NOT be associated with the value either as a language tag, as that is only available for  rdf:langString .

fields.name: oa:hasBody
fields.doc: The object of the relationship is a resource that is a body of the Annotation.

fields.name: oa:hasTarget
fields.doc: The relationship between an Annotation and its Target.

fields.name: oa:motivatedBy
fields.doc: The relationship between an Annotation and a Motivation that describes the reason for the Annotation's creation.

fields.name: oa:styledBy
fields.doc: A reference to a Stylesheet that should be used to apply styles to the Annotation rendering.

decls.name: oa:Choice
decls.doc: A subClass of  as:OrderedCollection  that conveys to a consuming application that it should select one of the resources in the  as:items  list to use, rather than all of them.  This is typically used to provide a choice of resources to render to the user, based on further supplied properties.  If the consuming application cannot determine the user's preference, then it should use the first in the

decls.name: oa:CssSelector
decls.doc: A CssSelector describes a Segment of interest in a representation that conforms to the Document Object Model through the use of the CSS selector specification.

decls.name: oa:CssStyle
decls.doc: A resource which describes styles for resources participating in the Annotation using CSS.

decls.name: oa:DataPositionSelector
decls.doc: DataPositionSelector describes a range of data by recording the start and end positions of the selection in the stream. Position 0 would be immediately before the first byte, position 1 would be immediately before the second byte, and so on. The start byte is thus included in the list, but the end byte is not.

decls.name: oa:Direction
decls.doc: A class to encapsulate the different text directions that a textual resource might take.  It is not used directly in the Annotation Model, only its three instances.

decls.name: oa:FragmentSelector
decls.doc: The FragmentSelector class is used to record the segment of a representation using the IRI fragment specification defined by the representation's media type.

decls.name: oa:HttpRequestState
decls.doc: The HttpRequestState class is used to record the HTTP request headers that a client SHOULD use to request the correct representation from the resource.

decls.name: oa:Motivation
decls.doc: The Motivation class is used to record the user's intent or motivation for the creation of the Annotation, or the inclusion of the body or target, that it is associated with.

decls.name: oa:RangeSelector
decls.doc: A Range Selector can be used to identify the beginning and the end of the selection by using other Selectors. The selection consists of everything from the beginning of the starting selector through to the beginning of the ending selector, but not including it.

fields.name: oa:hasEndSelector
fields.doc: The relationship between a RangeSelector and the Selector that describes the end position of the range.

fields.name: oa:hasStartSelector
fields.doc: The relationship between a RangeSelector and the Selector that describes the start position of the range.

decls.name: oa:ResourceSelection
decls.doc: Instances of the ResourceSelection class identify part (described by an oa:Selector) of another resource (referenced with oa:hasSource), possibly from a particular representation of a resource (described by an oa:State). Please note that ResourceSelection is not used directly in the Web Annotation model, but is provided as a separate class for further application profiles to use, separate from oa:

fields.name: oa:hasSelector
fields.doc: The object of the relationship is a Selector that describes the segment or region of interest within the source resource.  Please note that the domain ( oa:ResourceSelection ) is not used directly in the Web Annotation model.

fields.name: oa:hasSource
fields.doc: The resource that the ResourceSelection, or its subclass SpecificResource, is refined from, or more specific than. Please note that the domain ( oa:ResourceSelection ) is not used directly in the Web Annotation model.

fields.name: oa:hasState
fields.doc: The relationship between the ResourceSelection, or its subclass SpecificResource, and a State resource. Please note that the domain ( oa:ResourceSelection ) is not used directly in the Web Annotation model.

decls.name: oa:Selector
decls.doc: A resource which describes the segment of interest in a representation of a Source resource, indicated with oa:hasSelector from the Specific Resource. This class is not used directly in the Annotation model, only its subclasses.

decls.name: oa:SpecificResource
decls.doc: Instances of the SpecificResource class identify part of another resource (referenced with oa:hasSource), a particular representation of a resource, a resource with styling hints for renders, or any combination of these, as used within an Annotation.

fields.name: oa:hasScope
fields.doc: The scope or context in which the resource is used within the Annotation.

fields.name: oa:renderedVia
fields.doc: A system that was used by the application that created the Annotation to render the resource.

fields.name: oa:styleClass
fields.doc: The name of the class used in the CSS description referenced from the Annotation that should be applied to the Specific Resource.

decls.name: oa:State
decls.doc: A State describes the intended state of a resource as applied to the particular Annotation, and thus provides the information needed to retrieve the correct representation of that resource.

decls.name: oa:Style
decls.doc: A Style describes the intended styling of a resource as applied to the particular Annotation, and thus provides the information to ensure that rendering is consistent across implementations.

decls.name: oa:SvgSelector
decls.doc: An SvgSelector defines an area through the use of the Scalable Vector Graphics [SVG] standard. This allows the user to select a non-rectangular area of the content, such as a circle or polygon by describing the region using SVG. The SVG may be either embedded within the Annotation or referenced as an External Resource.

decls.name: oa:TextPositionSelector
decls.doc: The TextPositionSelector describes a range of text by recording the start and end positions of the selection in the stream. Position 0 would be immediately before the first character, position 1 would be immediately before the second character, and so on.

decls.name: oa:TextQuoteSelector
decls.doc: The TextQuoteSelector describes a range of text by copying it, and including some of the text immediately before (a prefix) and after (a suffix) it to distinguish between multiple copies of the same sequence of characters.

decls.name: oa:TimeState
decls.doc: A TimeState records the time at which the resource's state is appropriate for the Annotation, typically the time that the Annotation was created and/or a link to a persistent copy of the current version.

fields.name: oa:cachedSource
fields.doc: A object of the relationship is a copy of the Source resource's representation, appropriate for the Annotation.

fields.name: oa:sourceDate
fields.doc: The timestamp at which the Source resource should be interpreted as being applicable to the Annotation.

fields.name: oa:sourceDateEnd
fields.doc: The end timestamp of the interval over which the Source resource should be interpreted as being applicable to the Annotation.

fields.name: oa:sourceDateStart
fields.doc: The start timestamp of the interval over which the Source resource should be interpreted as being applicable to the Annotation.

decls.name: oa:XPathSelector
decls.doc: An XPathSelector is used to select elements and content within a resource that supports the Document Object Model via a specified XPath value.

decls.name: org
decls.doc: properties org states no domain in its own classes for

fields.name: org:basedAt
fields.doc: Indicates the site at which a person is based. We do not restrict the possibility that a person is based at multiple sites.

fields.name: org:hasMembership
fields.doc: Indicates a membership relationship that the Agent plays. Inverse of `org:member`.

fields.name: org:headOf
fields.doc: Indicates that a person is the leader or formal head of the Organization. This will normally mean that they are the root of the `org:reportsTo` (acyclic) graph, though an organization may have more than one head.

fields.name: org:holds
fields.doc: Indicates a Post held by some Agent.

fields.name: org:location
fields.doc: Gives a location description for a person within the organization, for example a _Mail Stop_ for internal posting purposes.

fields.name: org:memberOf
fields.doc: Indicates that a person is a member of the Organization with no indication of the nature of that membership or the role played. Note that the choice of property name is not meant to limit the property to only formal membership arrangements, it is also indended to cover related concepts such as affilliation or other involvement in the organization. Extensions can specialize this relationship to ind

decls.name: org:ChangeEvent
decls.doc: Represents an event which resulted in a major change to an organization such as a merger or complete restructuring. It is intended for situations where the resulting organization is sufficient distinct from the original organizations that it has a distinct identity and distinct URI. Extension vocabularies should define sub-classes of this to denote particular categories of event. The instant or in

fields.name: org:originalOrganization
fields.doc: Indicates one or more organizations that existed before the change event. Depending on the event they may or may not have continued to exist after the event. Inverse of `org:changedBy`.

fields.name: org:resultingOrganization
fields.doc: Indicates an organization which was created or changed as a result of the event. Inverse of `org:resultedFrom`.

decls.name: org:FormalOrganization
decls.doc: An Organization which is recognized in the world at large, in particular in legal jurisdictions, with associated rights and responsibilities. Examples include a Corporation, Charity, Government or Church. Note that this is a super class of `gr:BusinessEntity` and it is recommended to use the GoodRelations vocabulary to denote Business classifications such as DUNS or NAICS.

fields.name: org:hasRegisteredSite
fields.doc: Indicates the legally registered site for the organization, in many legal jurisdictions there is a requirement that FormalOrganizations such as Companies or Charities have such a primary designed site.

fields.name: org:hasUnit
fields.doc: Indicates a unit which is part of this Organization, e.g. a Department within a larger FormalOrganization. Inverse of `org:unitOf`.

decls.name: org:Membership
decls.doc: Indicates the nature of an Agent's membership of an organization. Represents an n-ary relation between an Agent, an Organization and a Role. It is possible to directly indicate membership, independent of the specific Role, through use of the `org:memberOf` property.

fields.name: org:member
fields.doc: Indicates the Person (or other Agent including Organization) involved in the Membership relationship. Inverse of `org:hasMembership`

fields.name: org:memberDuring
fields.doc: Optional property to indicate the interval for which the membership is/was valid.

fields.name: org:organization
fields.doc: Indicates Organization in which the Agent is a member.

fields.name: org:role
fields.doc: Indicates the Role that the Agent plays in a Membership relationship with an Organization.

decls.name: org:Organization
decls.doc: Represents a collection of people organized together into a community or other social, commercial or political structure. The group has some common purpose or reason for existence which goes beyond the set of people belonging to it and can act as an Agent. Organizations are often decomposable into hierarchical structures.  It is recommended that SKOS lexical labels should be used to label the Orga

fields.name: org:changedBy
fields.doc: Indicates a change event which resulted in a change to this organization. Depending on the event the organization may or may not have continued to exist after the event. Inverse of `org:originalOrganization`.

fields.name: org:classification
fields.doc: Indicates a classification for this Organization within some classification scheme. Extension vocabularies may wish to specialize this property to have a range corresponding to a specific `skos:ConceptScheme`. This property is under discussion and may be revised or removed - in many cases organizations are best categorized by defining a sub-class hierarchy in an extension vocabulary.

fields.name: org:hasMember
fields.doc: Indicates a person who is a member of the subject Organization. Inverse of `org:memberOf`, see that property for further clarification. Provided for compatibility with `foaf:member`.

fields.name: org:hasPost
fields.doc: Indicates a Post which exists within the Organization.

fields.name: org:hasPrimarySite
fields.doc: Indicates a primary site for the Organization, this is the default means by which an Organization can be contacted and is not necessarily the formal headquarters.

fields.name: org:hasSite
fields.doc: Indicates a site at which the Organization has some presence even if only indirect (e.g. virtual office or a professional service which is acting as the registered address for a company). Inverse of `org:siteOf`.

fields.name: org:hasSubOrganization
fields.doc: Represents hierarchical containment of Organizations or Organizational Units; indicates an organization which is a sub-part or child of this organization.  Inverse of `org:subOrganizationOf`.

fields.name: org:identifier
fields.doc: Gives an identifier, such as a company registration number, that can be used to used to uniquely identify the organization. Many different national and international identier schemes are available. The org ontology is neutral to which schemes are used. The particular identifier scheme should be indicated by the datatype of the identifier value.  Using datatypes to distinguish the notation scheme u

fields.name: org:linkedTo
fields.doc: Indicates an arbitrary relationship between two organizations. Specializations of this can be used to, for example, denote funding or supply chain relationships.

fields.name: org:purpose
fields.doc: Indicates the purpose of this Organization. There can be many purposes at different levels of abstraction but the nature of an organization is to have a reason for existence and this property is a means to document that reason. An Organization may have multiple purposes. It is recommended that the purpose be denoted by a controlled term or code list, ideally a `skos:Concept`. However, the range is

fields.name: org:resultedFrom
fields.doc: Indicates an event which resulted in this organization. Inverse of `org:resultingOrganization`.

fields.name: org:subOrganizationOf
fields.doc: Represents hierarchical containment of Organizations or OrganizationalUnits; indicates an Organization which contains this Organization. Inverse of `org:hasSubOrganization`.

fields.name: org:transitiveSubOrganizationOf
fields.doc: The transitive closure of subOrganizationOf, giving a representation of all organizations that contain this one. Note that technically this is a super property of the transitive closure so it could contain additional assertions but such usage is discouraged.

decls.name: org:OrganizationalCollaboration
decls.doc: A collaboration between two or more Organizations such as a project. It meets the criteria for being an Organization in that it has an identity and defining purpose independent of its particular members but is neither a formally recognized legal entity nor a sub-unit within some larger organization. Might typically have a shorter lifetime than the Organizations within it, but not necessarily. All

decls.name: org:OrganizationalUnit
decls.doc: An Organization such as a University Support Unit which is part of some larger FormalOrganization and only has full recognition within the context of that FormalOrganization, it is not a Legal Entity in its own right. Units can be large and complex containing other Units and even FormalOrganizations. Alternative names: _OU_ _Unit_ _Department_

fields.name: org:unitOf
fields.doc: Indicates an Organization of which this Unit is a part, e.g. a Department within a larger FormalOrganization. This is the inverse of `org:hasUnit`.

decls.name: org:Post
decls.doc: A Post represents some position within an organization that exists independently of the person or persons filling it. Posts may be used to represent situations where a person is a member of an organization ex officio (for example the Secretary of State for Scotland is part of UK Cabinet by virtue of being Secretary of State for Scotland, not as an individual person). A post can be held by multiple

fields.name: org:heldBy
fields.doc: Indicates an Agent which holds a Post.

fields.name: org:postIn
fields.doc: Indicates the Organization in which the Post exists.

fields.name: org:reportsTo
fields.doc: Indicates a reporting relationship as might be depicted on an organizational chart. The precise semantics of the reporting relationship will vary by organization but is intended to encompass both direct supervisory relationships (e.g. carrying objective and salary setting authority) and more general reporting or accountability relationships (e.g. so called _dotted line_ reporting).

fields.name: org:role
fields.doc: Indicates the Role that the Agent plays in a Membership relationship with an Organization.

decls.name: org:Role
decls.doc: Denotes a role that a Person or other Agent can take in an organization. Instances of this class describe the abstract role; to denote a specific instance of a person playing that role in a specific organization use an instance of `org:Membership`. It is common for roles to be arranged in some taxonomic structure and we use SKOS to represent that. The normal SKOS lexical properties should be used

fields.name: org:remuneration
fields.doc: Indicates a salary or other reward associated with the role. Typically this will be denoted using an existing representation scheme such as `gr:PriceSpecification` but the range is left open to allow applications to specialize it (e.g. to remunerationInGBP).

fields.name: org:roleProperty
fields.doc: This is a metalevel property which is used to annotate an `org:Role` instance with a sub-property of `org:memberOf` that can be used to directly indicate the role for easy of query. The intended semantics is a Membership relation involving the Role implies the existence of a direct property relationship through an inference rule of the form:  `{ [] org:member ?p; org:organization ?o; org:role [org

decls.name: org:Site
decls.doc: An office or other premise at which the organization is located. Many organizations are spread across multiple sites and many sites will host multiple locations. In most cases a Site will be a physical location. However, we don't exclude the possibility of non-physical sites such as a virtual office with an associated post box and phone reception service. Extensions may provide subclasses to denot

fields.name: org:siteAddress
fields.doc: Indicates an address for the site in a suitable encoding. Use of vCard (using the http://www.w3.org/TR/vcard-rdf/ vocabulary) is encouraged but the range is left open to allow other encodings to be used. The address may include email, telephone, and geo-location information and is not restricted to a physical address.

fields.name: org:siteOf
fields.doc: Indicates an Organization which has some presence at the given site. This is the inverse of `org:hasSite`.

decls.name: owl
decls.doc: properties owl states no domain in its own classes for

fields.name: owl:annotatedProperty
fields.doc: The property that determines the predicate of an annotated axiom or annotated annotation.

fields.name: owl:annotatedSource
fields.doc: The property that determines the subject of an annotated axiom or annotated annotation.

fields.name: owl:annotatedTarget
fields.doc: The property that determines the object of an annotated axiom or annotated annotation.

fields.name: owl:bottomDataProperty
fields.doc: The data property that does not relate any individual to any data value.

fields.name: owl:bottomObjectProperty
fields.doc: The object property that does not relate any two individuals.

fields.name: owl:datatypeComplementOf
fields.doc: The property that determines that a given data range is the complement of another data range with respect to the data domain.

fields.name: owl:deprecated
fields.doc: The annotation property that indicates that a given entity has been deprecated.

fields.name: owl:differentFrom
fields.doc: The property that determines that two given individuals are different.

fields.name: owl:equivalentClass
fields.doc: The property that determines that two given classes are equivalent, and that is used to specify datatype definitions.

fields.name: owl:equivalentProperty
fields.doc: The property that determines that two given properties are equivalent.

fields.name: owl:intersectionOf
fields.doc: The property that determines the collection of classes or data ranges that build an intersection.

fields.name: owl:members
fields.doc: The property that determines the collection of members in either a owl:AllDifferent, owl:AllDisjointClasses or owl:AllDisjointProperties axiom.

fields.name: owl:onDatatype
fields.doc: The property that determines the datatype that a datatype restriction refers to.

fields.name: owl:oneOf
fields.doc: The property that determines the collection of individuals or data values that build an enumeration.

fields.name: owl:propertyDisjointWith
fields.doc: The property that determines that two given properties are disjoint.

fields.name: owl:sameAs
fields.doc: The property that determines that two given individuals are equal.

fields.name: owl:topDataProperty
fields.doc: The data property that relates every individual to every data value.

fields.name: owl:topObjectProperty
fields.doc: The object property that relates every two individuals.

fields.name: owl:unionOf
fields.doc: The property that determines the collection of classes or data ranges that build a union.

fields.name: owl:versionInfo
fields.doc: The annotation property that provides version information for an ontology or another OWL construct.

fields.name: owl:withRestrictions
fields.doc: The property that determines the collection of facet-value pairs that define a datatype restriction.

decls.name: owl:AllDifferent
decls.doc: The class of collections of pairwise different individuals.

fields.name: owl:distinctMembers
fields.doc: The property that determines the collection of pairwise different individuals in a owl:AllDifferent axiom.

decls.name: owl:AllDisjointClasses
decls.doc: The class of collections of pairwise disjoint classes.

decls.name: owl:AllDisjointProperties
decls.doc: The class of collections of pairwise disjoint properties.

decls.name: prov
decls.doc: properties prov states no domain in its own classes for

fields.name: prov:category
fields.doc: Classify prov-o terms into three categories, including 'starting-point', 'qualifed', and 'extended'. This classification is used by the prov-o html document to gently introduce prov-o terms to its users.

fields.name: prov:component
fields.doc: Classify prov-o terms into six components according to prov-dm, including 'agents-responsibility', 'alternate', 'annotations', 'collections', 'derivations', and 'entities-activities'. This classification is used so that readers of prov-o specification can find its correspondence with the prov-dm specification.

fields.name: prov:constraints
fields.doc: A reference to the principal section of the PROV-CONSTRAINTS document that describes this concept.

fields.name: prov:definition
fields.doc: A definition quoted from PROV-DM or PROV-CONSTRAINTS that describes the concept expressed with this OWL term.

fields.name: prov:describesService
fields.doc: relates a generic provenance query service resource (type prov:ServiceDescription) to a specific query service description (e.g. a prov:DirectQueryService or a sd:Service).

fields.name: prov:dm
fields.doc: A reference to the principal section of the PROV-DM document that describes this concept.

fields.name: prov:editorialNote
fields.doc: A note by the OWL development team about how this term expresses the PROV-DM concept, or how it should be used in context of semantic web or linked data.

fields.name: prov:editorsDefinition
fields.doc: When the prov-o term does not have a definition drawn from prov-dm, and the prov-o editor provides one.

fields.name: prov:has_anchor
fields.doc: Indicates anchor URI for a potentially dynamic resource instance.

fields.name: prov:has_provenance
fields.doc: Indicates a provenance-URI for a resource; the resource identified by this property presents a provenance record about its subject or anchor resource.

fields.name: prov:has_query_service
fields.doc: Indicates a provenance query service that can access provenance related to its subject or anchor resource.

fields.name: prov:inverse
fields.doc: PROV-O does not define all property inverses. The directionalities defined in PROV-O should be given preference over those not defined. However, if users wish to name the inverse of a PROV-O property, the local name given by prov:inverse should be used.

fields.name: prov:n
fields.doc: A reference to the principal section of the PROV-M document that describes this concept.

fields.name: prov:order
fields.doc: The position that this OWL term should be listed within documentation. The scope of the documentation (e.g., among all terms, among terms within a prov:category, among properties applying to a particular class, etc.) is unspecified.

fields.name: prov:pingback
fields.doc: Relates a resource to a provenance pingback service that may receive additional provenance links about the resource.

fields.name: prov:provenanceUriTemplate
fields.doc: Relates a provenance service to a URI template string for constructing provenance-URIs.

fields.name: prov:qualifiedForm
fields.doc: This annotation property links a subproperty of prov:wasInfluencedBy with the subclass of prov:Influence and the qualifying property that are used to qualify it.

fields.name: prov:unqualifiedForm
fields.doc: Classes and properties used to qualify relationships are annotated with prov:unqualifiedForm to indicate the property used to assert an unqualified provenance relation.

fields.name: prov:atLocation
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:endedAtTime
fields.doc: The time at which an activity ended. See also prov:startedAtTime.

fields.name: prov:qualifiedAssociation
fields.doc: If this Activity prov:wasAssociatedWith Agent :ag, then it can qualify the Association using prov:qualifiedAssociation [ a prov:Association;  prov:agent :ag; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedCommunication
fields.doc: If this Activity prov:wasInformedBy Activity :a, then it can qualify how it was influenced using prov:qualifiedCommunication [ a prov:Communication;  prov:activity :a; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedEnd
fields.doc: If this Activity prov:wasEndedBy Entity :e1, then it can qualify how it was ended using prov:qualifiedEnd [ a prov:End;  prov:entity :e1; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedInfluence
fields.doc: Because prov:qualifiedInfluence is a broad relation, the more specific relations (qualifiedCommunication, qualifiedDelegation, qualifiedEnd, etc.) should be used when applicable.

fields.name: prov:qualifiedStart
fields.doc: If this Activity prov:wasStartedBy Entity :e1, then it can qualify how it was started using prov:qualifiedStart [ a prov:Start;  prov:entity :e1; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedUsage
fields.doc: If this Activity prov:used Entity :e, then it can qualify how it used it using prov:qualifiedUsage [ a prov:Usage; prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:startedAtTime
fields.doc: The time at which an activity started. See also prov:endedAtTime.

fields.name: prov:used
fields.doc: A prov:Entity that was used by this prov:Activity. For example, :baking prov:used :spoon, :egg, :oven .

fields.name: prov:wasAssociatedWith
fields.doc: An prov:Agent that had some (unspecified) responsibility for the occurrence of this prov:Activity.

fields.name: prov:wasEndedBy
fields.doc: End is when an activity is deemed to have ended. An end may refer to an entity, known as trigger, that terminated the activity.

fields.name: prov:wasInfluencedBy
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:wasInformedBy
fields.doc: An activity a2 is dependent on or informed by another activity a1, by way of some unspecified entity that is generated by a1 and used by a2.

fields.name: prov:wasStartedBy
fields.doc: Start is when an activity is deemed to have started. A start may refer to an entity, known as trigger, that initiated the activity.

decls.name: prov:ActivityInfluence
decls.doc: It is not recommended that the type ActivityInfluence be asserted without also asserting one of its more specific subclasses.

fields.name: prov:hadActivity
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:actedOnBehalfOf
fields.doc: An object property to express the accountability of an agent towards another agent. The subordinate agent acted on behalf of the responsible agent in an actual activity.

fields.name: prov:atLocation
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:qualifiedDelegation
fields.doc: If this Agent prov:actedOnBehalfOf Agent :ag, then it can qualify how with prov:qualifiedResponsibility [ a prov:Responsibility;  prov:agent :ag; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedInfluence
fields.doc: Because prov:qualifiedInfluence is a broad relation, the more specific relations (qualifiedCommunication, qualifiedDelegation, qualifiedEnd, etc.) should be used when applicable.

fields.name: prov:wasInfluencedBy
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

decls.name: prov:AgentInfluence
decls.doc: It is not recommended that the type AgentInfluence be asserted without also asserting one of its more specific subclasses.

decls.name: prov:Association
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Association provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasAssociatedWith relation from an prov:Activity to some prov:Agent that had some responsiblity for it. For example, :baking prov:wasAssociatedWith :baker; prov:qualifiedAssociation [ a prov:Association; prov:agent :baker; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:hadPlan
fields.doc: The _optional_ Plan adopted by an Agent in Association with some Activity. Plan specifications are out of the scope of this specification.

fields.name: prov:hadRole
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

decls.name: prov:Attribution
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Attribution provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasAttributedTo relation from an prov:Entity to some prov:Agent that had some responsible for it. For example, :cake prov:wasAttributedTo :baker; prov:qualifiedAttribution [ a prov:Attribution; prov:entity :baker; :foo :bar ].

decls.name: prov:Bundle
decls.doc: Note that there are kinds of bundles (e.g. handwritten letters, audio recordings, etc.) that are not expressed in PROV-O, but can be still be described by PROV-O.

decls.name: prov:Communication
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Communication provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasInformedBy relation from an informed prov:Activity to the prov:Activity that informed it. For example, :you_jumping_off_bridge prov:wasInformedBy :everyone_else_jumping_off_bridge; prov:qualifiedCommunication [ a prov:Communication; prov:activity :everyone_else_jumping_off_bridge; :foo :bar ].

decls.name: prov:Delegation
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Delegation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:actedOnBehalfOf relation from a performing prov:Agent to some prov:Agent for whom it was performed. For example, :mixing prov:wasAssociatedWith :toddler . :toddler prov:actedOnBehalfOf :mother; prov:qualifiedDelegation [ a prov:Delegation; prov:entity :mother; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:hadActivity
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

decls.name: prov:Derivation
decls.doc: The more specific forms of prov:Derivation (i.e., prov:Revision, prov:Quotation, prov:PrimarySource) should be asserted if they apply.

fields.name: prov:hadActivity
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:hadGeneration
fields.doc: The _optional_ Generation involved in an Entity's Derivation.

fields.name: prov:hadUsage
fields.doc: The _optional_ Usage involved in an Entity's Derivation.

decls.name: prov:Dictionary
decls.doc: This concept allows for the provenance of the dictionary, but also of its constituents to be expressed. Such a notion of dictionary corresponds to a wide variety of concrete data structures, such as a maps or associative arrays.

decls.name: prov:DirectQueryService
decls.doc: Type for a generic provenance query service. Mainly for use in RDF provenance query service descriptions, to facilitate discovery in linked data environments.

decls.name: prov:End
decls.doc: An instance of prov:End provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasEndedBy relation from some ended prov:Activity to an prov:Entity that ended it. For example, :ball_game prov:wasEndedBy :buzzer; prov:qualifiedEnd [ a prov:End; prov:entity :buzzer; :foo :bar; prov:atTime '2012-03-09T08:05:08-05:00'^^xsd:dateTime ].

fields.name: prov:hadActivity
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:asInBundle
fields.doc: prov:asInBundle is used to specify which bundle the general entity of a prov:mentionOf property is described.

fields.name: prov:atLocation
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:generatedAtTime
fields.doc: The time at which an entity was completely created and is available for use.

fields.name: prov:invalidatedAtTime
fields.doc: The time at which an entity was invalidated (i.e., no longer usable).

fields.name: prov:mentionOf
fields.doc: prov:mentionOf is used to specialize an entity as described in another bundle. It is to be used in conjuction with prov:asInBundle.

fields.name: prov:qualifiedAttribution
fields.doc: If this Entity prov:wasAttributedTo Agent :ag, then it can qualify how it was influenced using prov:qualifiedAttribution [ a prov:Attribution;  prov:agent :ag; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedDerivation
fields.doc: If this Entity prov:wasDerivedFrom Entity :e, then it can qualify how it was derived using prov:qualifiedDerivation [ a prov:Derivation;  prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedGeneration
fields.doc: If this Activity prov:generated Entity :e, then it can qualify how it performed the Generation using prov:qualifiedGeneration [ a prov:Generation;  prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedInfluence
fields.doc: Because prov:qualifiedInfluence is a broad relation, the more specific relations (qualifiedCommunication, qualifiedDelegation, qualifiedEnd, etc.) should be used when applicable.

fields.name: prov:qualifiedInvalidation
fields.doc: If this Entity prov:wasInvalidatedBy Activity :a, then it can qualify how it was invalidated using prov:qualifiedInvalidation [ a prov:Invalidation;  prov:activity :a; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedPrimarySource
fields.doc: If this Entity prov:hadPrimarySource Entity :e, then it can qualify how using prov:qualifiedPrimarySource [ a prov:PrimarySource; prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedQuotation
fields.doc: If this Entity prov:wasQuotedFrom Entity :e, then it can qualify how using prov:qualifiedQuotation [ a prov:Quotation;  prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:qualifiedRevision
fields.doc: If this Entity prov:wasRevisionOf Entity :e, then it can qualify how it was revised using prov:qualifiedRevision [ a prov:Revision;  prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

fields.name: prov:wasAttributedTo
fields.doc: Attribution is the ascribing of an entity to an agent.

fields.name: prov:wasDerivedFrom
fields.doc: The more specific subproperties of prov:wasDerivedFrom (i.e., prov:wasQuotedFrom, prov:wasRevisionOf, prov:hadPrimarySource) should be used when applicable.

fields.name: prov:wasInfluencedBy
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:wasQuotedFrom
fields.doc: An entity is derived from an original entity by copying, or 'quoting', some or all of it.

fields.name: prov:wasRevisionOf
fields.doc: A revision is a derivation that revises an entity into a revised version.

decls.name: prov:EntityInfluence
decls.doc: It is not recommended that the type EntityInfluence be asserted without also asserting one of its more specific subclasses.

decls.name: prov:Generation
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Generation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasGeneratedBy relation from a generated prov:Entity to the prov:Activity that generated it. For example, :cake prov:wasGeneratedBy :baking; prov:qualifiedGeneration [ a prov:Generation; prov:activity :baking; :foo :bar ].

decls.name: prov:Influence
decls.doc: Because prov:Influence is a broad relation, its most specific subclasses (e.g. prov:Communication, prov:Delegation, prov:End, prov:Revision, etc.) should be used when applicable.

fields.name: prov:hadActivity
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:hadRole
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:influencer
fields.doc: Subproperties of prov:influencer are used to cite the object of an unqualified PROV-O triple whose predicate is a subproperty of prov:wasInfluencedBy (e.g. prov:used, prov:wasGeneratedBy). prov:influencer is used much like rdf:object is used.

decls.name: prov:InstantaneousEvent
decls.doc: An instantaneous event, or event for short, happens in the world and marks a change in the world, in its activities and in its entities. The term 'event' is commonly used in process algebra with a similar meaning. Events represent communications or interactions; they are assumed to be atomic and instantaneous.

fields.name: prov:atLocation
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

fields.name: prov:atTime
fields.doc: The time at which an InstantaneousEvent occurred, in the form of xsd:dateTime.

fields.name: prov:hadRole
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

decls.name: prov:Invalidation
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Invalidation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasInvalidatedBy relation from an invalidated prov:Entity to the prov:Activity that invalidated it. For example, :uncracked_egg prov:wasInvalidatedBy :baking; prov:qualifiedInvalidation [ a prov:Invalidation; prov:activity :baking; :foo :bar ].

decls.name: prov:Plan
decls.doc: There exist no prescriptive requirement on the nature of plans, their representation, the actions or steps they consist of, or their intended goals. Since plans may evolve over time, it may become necessary to track their provenance, so plans themselves are entities. Representing the plan explicitly in the provenance can be useful for various tasks: for example, to validate the execution as repres

decls.name: prov:PrimarySource
decls.doc: An instance of prov:PrimarySource provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:hadPrimarySource relation from some secondary prov:Entity to an earlier, primary prov:Entity. For example, :blog prov:hadPrimarySource :newsArticle; prov:qualifiedPrimarySource [ a prov:PrimarySource; prov:entity :newsArticle; :foo :bar ] .

decls.name: prov:Quotation
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Quotation provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasQuotedFrom relation from some taken prov:Entity from an earlier, larger prov:Entity. For example, :here_is_looking_at_you_kid prov:wasQuotedFrom :casablanca_script; prov:qualifiedQuotation [ a prov:Quotation; prov:entity :casablanca_script; :foo :bar ].

decls.name: prov:Revision
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Revision provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasRevisionOf relation from some newer prov:Entity to an earlier prov:Entity. For example, :draft_2 prov:wasRevisionOf :draft_1; prov:qualifiedRevision [ a prov:Revision; prov:entity :draft_1; :foo :bar ].

decls.name: prov:ServiceDescription
decls.doc: Type for a generic provenance query service. Mainly for use in RDF provenance query service descriptions, to facilitate discovery in linked data environments.

decls.name: prov:Start
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Start provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:wasStartedBy relation from some started prov:Activity to an prov:Entity that started it. For example, :foot_race prov:wasStartedBy :bang; prov:qualifiedStart [ a prov:Start; prov:entity :bang; :foo :bar; prov:atTime '2012-03-09T08:05:08-05:00'^^xsd:dateTime ] .

fields.name: prov:hadActivity
fields.doc: This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

decls.name: prov:Usage
decls.doc: An instance of prov:Usage provides additional descriptions about the binary prov:used relation from some prov:Activity to an prov:Entity that it used. For example, :keynote prov:used :podium; prov:qualifiedUsage [ a prov:Usage; prov:entity :podium; :foo :bar ].

decls.doc: A word, name, acronym, phrase, etc. with a formal definition. Often used in the context of category or subject classification, glossaries or dictionaries, product or creative work types, etc. Use the name property for the term being defined, use termCode if the term has an alpha-numeric code allocated, use description to provide the definition of the term. Use the about property to specify what th

fields.name: schema:about
fields.doc: The subject matter of an object.

fields.name: schema:inDefinedTermSet
fields.doc: A [[DefinedTermSet]] that contains this term.

fields.name: schema:termCode

decls.name: schema:MediaObject
decls.doc: A media object, such as an image, video, audio, or text object embedded in a web page or a downloadable dataset i.e. DataDownload. Note that a creative work may have many media objects associated with it on the same web page. For example, a page about a single song (MusicRecording) may have a music video (VideoObject), and a high and low bandwidth audio stream (2 AudioObject's).

fields.name: schema:associatedArticle
fields.doc: A NewsArticle associated with the Media Object.

fields.name: schema:bitrate
fields.doc: The bitrate of the media object.

fields.name: schema:contentSize

fields.doc: Relates a collection to one of its members.

decls.doc: An idea or notion; a unit of thought.

fields.name: skos:broadMatch
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: skos:broadMatch is used to state a hierarchical mapping link between two conceptual resources in different concept schemes.

fields.name: skos:broader
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: Relates a concept to a concept that is more general in meaning.

fields.name: skos:broaderTransitive
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: skos:broaderTransitive is a transitive superproperty of skos:broader.

fields.name: skos:closeMatch
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: skos:closeMatch is used to link two concepts that are sufficiently similar that they can be used interchangeably in some information retrieval applications. In order to avoid the possibility of "compound errors" when combining mappings across more than two concept schemes, skos:closeMatch is not declared to be a transitive property.

fields.name: skos:exactMatch
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: skos:exactMatch is used to link two concepts, indicating a high degree of confidence that the concepts can be used interchangeably across a wide range of information retrieval applications. skos:exactMatch is a transitive property, and is a sub-property of skos:closeMatch.

fields.name: skos:mappingRelation
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: Relates two concepts coming, by convention, from different schemes, and that have comparable meanings

fields.name: skos:narrowMatch
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: skos:narrowMatch is used to state a hierarchical mapping link between two conceptual resources in different concept schemes.

fields.name: skos:narrower
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: Relates a concept to a concept that is more specific in meaning.

fields.name: skos:narrowerTransitive
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: skos:narrowerTransitive is a transitive superproperty of skos:narrower.

fields.name: skos:related
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: Relates a concept to a concept with which there is an associative semantic relationship.

fields.name: skos:relatedMatch
fields.constraint: domain via skos:semanticRelation, range via skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: skos:relatedMatch is used to state an associative mapping link between two conceptual resources in different concept schemes.

fields.name: skos:semanticRelation
fields.doc: Links a concept to a concept related by meaning.

fields.name: skos:topConceptOf
fields.doc: Relates a concept to the concept scheme that it is a top level concept of.

fields.doc: Relates an ordered collection to the RDF list containing its members.
